Department of Physics
A degree in physics provides valuable research and critical thinking skills which prepare students for a variety of careers. We offer physics majors and graduate students a high quality physics education with small classes in a research oriented environment. The programs are implemented by faculty who are excellent teachers and also maintain active, world-class research programs.
Our small class sizes, ground-breaking research opportunities, and one-on-one interaction with world class professors are just a few reasons to join our program.

Physics in the News
USU's Science Unwrapped Explores 'Physics of Ballet' on Oct. 16
USU Today | October 13, 2026
What do physics and ballet have in common? A lot! Utah State University physicist Tonya Triplett and Cache Valley dancer Becky Erickson will team up Friday at USU’s Science Unwrapped to demonstrate the beautiful, complex interplay of science and dance. They will present “The Physics of Ballet” at 7 p.m. in the Eccles Science Learning Center Emert Auditorium, Room ESLC 130, on the Logan campus.

Scaling Up, Out, Across: USU Physicist Explores Light as Pathway to Quantum Computing
USU Today | September 18, 2026
Nanophotonics researcher and new faculty member Feng Pan, recently honored with a top research paper award from Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory's Molecular Foundry, seeks student researchers for varied project opportunities.
Read More
USU's Science Unwrapped Explores Hidden Physics Behind Artistic Expression on Sept. 18
USU Today | September 14, 2026
Utah State University physicist David Smith is the featured speaker at the free, family friendly event, which begins at 7 p.m. in the Eccles Science Learning Center on the Logan campus. All ages are welcome.
